devsec-bot: ALERT: SBOM checksum mismatch detected for package 'libproto@1.4.2' in image redwood/runtime:2026-03-15. Possible supply-chain tampering or vendor repackaging. Scan ID: scan-9f3b.

devsec-bot: Details:
```
SBOM entry: libproto@1.4.2
expected_sha256: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
observed_sha256: 3a7bd3c5f1a9b8e4a1b2c7d9e2f4a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f
image: registry.redwood/internal/runtime:2026-03-15
layer: /usr/lib/libproto.so
confidence: high
```

alyssa: dropping in — which environments are affected? prod? :thinking_face:

mike: can we confirm this is the same libproto referenced by our model-runtime container? I can pull image and diff layers.

mike: running quick check: `skopeo copy docker://registry.redwood/internal/runtime:2026-03-15 dir:/tmp/img && tar -xOf /tmp/img/manifest.json`

oncall: I've marked the image as quarantined in the registry (tagged +quarantine) and disabled pulls for non-admins. Notifying infra to pause any rollout using that tag.

oncall: registry action id: action-4472.

sophie: do we have a signed SBOM for that build? If SBOMs are cosign-attested we can verify provenance. If not, higher risk.

devsec-bot: SBOM signature check: `cosign verify-blob --signature sbom.sig sbom.json` -> signature missing. Provenance: build metadata shows git ref `feature/opt-bundles` from 2026-03-14, builder image builder-v2. No detached signature present.

jordan: I can take triage. Steps I want approved: 1) Keep image quarantined 2) Roll back any deployed pins to previous verified image 3) Run full SBOM regeneration and binary diffs 4) Open vendor query with upstream. Approve?

alyssa: +1 to Jordan's plan. Also add: collect runtime telemetry for containers that used that image in last 48h (calls to KMS, unusual outbound).

mike: I ran `sha256sum` on the extracted libproto.so from the quarantined image and it matches observed_sha256 above. So it is different than expected release artifact.

sophie: tagging this incident as P2 for now but escalate to P1 if we see unknown outbound connections or secrets exfil attempts. I'll start the compliance log to capture audit events and KMS access records.

devsec-bot: Noted: created incident incident-20260315-9f3b and linked scan-9f3b. Audit log query template:
```
# get KMS access for service accounts
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_key" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt" AND timestamp>="2026-03-13T00:00:00Z"' --limit 100
```

oncall: I've alerted SRE to halt any autoscaling that would spin up nodes pulling that image.

jordan: I'll start the binary diff and vendor outreach. If vendor confirms repackaging, we need CVE-triage flow and an advisory for customers. Who owns external comms?

alyssa: Product comms should partner with security. I'll loop in product-ops and legal once we have vendor response. For now, keep internal-only.

mike: checklist I ran so far:
- quarantined image: yes
- collect sbom + extracted binary: yes
- compare checksums: mismatch
- cosign verify: no signature
- network telemetry query started: yes

sophie: good. Jordan, ping here with findings. If you need expanded forensics (memory, host artifacts), call-forensics.

devsec-bot: Reminder: create a long-term remediation ticket to require SBOM signing and cosign verification in CI for all runtime images.

alyssa: agreed. For post-mortem: add enforcement of KMS-backed signing keys and RBAC to restrict who can push signed SBOMs.

jordan: starting triage now — will post updates. :mag:
